decisions.reason: The panel power-control clause is an independent decision already represented by its same-message INTRODUCE; changing DCDC1 voltage does not alter the connector or button behavior.
The DCDC1 adjustment compensates for the existing Schottky OR-ing path but does not change the standalone LDO, its activation condition, or the shared rail's required 3.3V output.
The monitor remains after the Schottky diodes and continues measuring the same regulated 3.3V rail; its IC, channels, position, and measurement coverage are unchanged.
The source preserves the post-OR-ing system rail at 3.3V, so the interboard connector pinouts and power-distribution topology remain valid unchanged.
The sensor board still receives and distributes a 3.3V rail; the upstream pre-diode DCDC1 setting does not change any sensor connector or supply requirement.
The source changes the AXP2101 DCDC1 path for the 3.3V rail and does not alter the independently switched 5V boost rail.
DCDC1 remains the power-board-connected source for the system 3.3V rail, and the battery, USB, VMID, and VSYS power-path attributes remain unchanged.
The DCDC1 compensation decision does not change the ESP32 BOOT or reset controls or their capacitance values.
The selected ESP32-S3 module is unaffected by the upstream DCDC1 voltage compensation.
The source concerns power-rail regulation and does not change the USB-C data or programming interface.
The LED board's part selection, package, color format, and board composition are unaffected by the DCDC1 3.4V pre-diode setting.
The source explicitly maintains the system rail at 3.3V after the Schottky drop, so the I2C pull-up voltage assumptions and signal-conditioning requirements remain unchanged.
